questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my study destination there where several aspects I found important. I preferebly wanted to go to a place with english as the first language. Second I wanted to go somewhere that I could explore nature and historic sites. It was also important for me to go to a university with an active social life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really good experience. I think I got exactly what I hoped for when applying for the exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. There was a lot of information online and the exchange students also got assigned a counselor that we could ask about anything related to courses and university life.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I do not think I received any assistance when I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Really satisfied. It was easy to get help via. email or at the university website.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy at all. As an exchange student only staying for one semester the university cannot promise that they have a housing possibility for you. The private housing market was very difficult to get into as an international student and I was a bit frustrated that the university was not more helpfull.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most of the student accommodations are quite expensive but most of them have good locations. It is a nice way to meet other students. But most of the students living there are first years.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to find information about courses and requirements for the courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You register for courses online. You choose a list of courses and prioritize them. 
A couple of weeks before the semester begin you can view your courses on your university profile. You are able to make course changes until two weeks after semester start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Brochures, the visiting student counselor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose courses you think sound interesting. And take the possibilities to change course if you change your mind during the first two weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Could have been nice with more economics courses to choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses I had was quite close to the courses at UCPH. Maybe a bit easier and the curriculum was somewhat smaller than the usual course a UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The same with both lectures and teaching hours. The biggest difference was that the university did midterm exams in the middle of the semester that counted some percentage in your total mark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Organisational Behaviour 
Structural transformation in the labour market
Economics of inequality

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Structural transformation in the labour market was a really interesting and well planned course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was unexpected that the housing would be so expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general grocery shopping and going out for dinner was much cheaper than in CPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was possibilities for everyone depending on your interests.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds. There was over a 100 different clubs or societies to join. All from mountaineering club, book clubs and different activist societies. The societies where easy to join and most of them had many events during the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the hillwalking society which I can really recommend! They had many events during the semester where you got to meet many other students from all over the world. Both other exchange students but also local students. They offered weekly meetings at a pub and hiking trips in the highlands every other weekend. It was a really nice and affordable way to explore the nature and meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go and explore the highlands and the islands in the north west. It is easy to rent a car og join a bus trip and go out to explore. If you enjoy hiking or other outdoor activity there are amazing possibilities. In the city there is a lot to explore as well and a lot of the museums and tours are free.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society or a club and go to the events and meetups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really notice any differences that I found challenging. I really like the scottish culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The scottish people are really nice and welcoming. I really appreciated that it was easy to get in touch with people and that they where very down to earth.  Also I really enjoyed the pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you want to find private accommodation you should begin early on. You can join groups on facebook to find rooms etc. 
2. Definitely join a society (or more) (there is probably one for your education as well). 
3. Enjoy that the university has a lot of social and educational events but remember to sign up!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is hard to choose since I found the whole experience very rewarding. It was rewarding to study in another country with different teaching methods and collaborate with other students from all over the world. It has been very rewarding to move abroad, find new friends and get a lot of new experiences. It was very rewarding for me to be able to explore the highlands and learn about the scottish history.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My biggest challenge was that I wished that the semester would have been longer. I feel like it all went by very fast. Also it was challenging but also very rewarding to be much more on my own than I am used to from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
